cards.title: Childhood sexual abuse in families: supporting victims
cards.body: Make the victim feel safe and able to talk at their own pace. Consider any danger the perpetrator currently presents to younger family members.

cards.title: Taking toddlers to music festivals adds family magic
cards.body: Families with children enhance the experience of music festivals rather than spoil them. Parents can successfully navigate events while twins and young children thrive in the festive atmosphere.

cards.title: Preparing for your son's university departure
cards.body: Empty nesting can be emotionally harder than expected, even for parents who know it's natural. Watching your first-born leave home with new saucepans triggers surprising feelings of loss.

cards.title: Parallel parenting vs co-parenting after divorce
cards.body: Estranged parents often share less information with each other, but some details are essential to share. The approach you take affects children's wellbeing and parental cooperation.

cards.title: Lower your child's emotional intensity effectively
cards.body: Being the thermostat rather than the thermometer can regulate your child's emotional state. This approach works across different ages and prevents escalation of intense moments.

cards.title: Screens and childhood development matter
cards.body: Today's kindergartners have never known a screen-free world, making protection of reading and play time crucial. Human connection from birth remains essential despite technology's pervasiveness.

cards.title: Narcissistic parenting and its long-term effects
cards.body: Growing up feeling not good enough often stems from narcissistic parenting patterns. New research shows recovery is possible through understanding and establishing healthier boundaries.

cards.title: Tickling explained: why self-tickling doesn't work
cards.body: Self-generated touch is expected by the brain, making self-tickling nearly impossible. Tickling stimuli work best when they're unexpected.
